prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: ultra-photoreal architectural editorial photograph for a luxury tile studio homepage journey, wide landscape 16:9.
Input image 1 is the exact owner-supplied Diamond lattice tile sample, not loose style inspiration. Preserve its particular fine dark-brown / charcoal angular diamond-and-line drawing, warm taupe and pale stone-color field, complete square proportions, original border and subdued surface character. The design has specific interlocking diagonal lozenge cells, varied little geometric forms inside them, and fine doubled lines. Do not replace it with generic lattice, change colors, add relief, or redesign individual motifs.
Primary request: Create a sophisticated, spacious residential living room in a quiet contemporary stone villa. The exact supplied tile pattern is repeated faithfully in an expansive architectural feature wall occupying the central rear wall, made from complete identical square tile faces with fine joints. This is naturally installed tile, not framed artwork. In the foreground, a low sculptural olive-grey linen sofa occupies the right lower third and a slim walnut and limestone coffee table sits to its left. A single low pale boucle armchair is near the extreme left margin, leaving nearly the entire tile wall unobstructed. Warm ivory plaster walls and generous pale limestone floor, exposed dark oak ceiling beams, large tall glazed opening at left with a private garden beyond, soft sheer curtain. Restrained and very luxurious with beautiful believable materials.
Composition: Eye-level wide editorial photograph, 28mm architectural lens, carefully straight verticals, real room proportions and depth. The dominant tile feature wall stays in the central 25–75 percent of the image so a mobile portrait crop still shows the pattern and a corner of the sofa. View nearly frontal to the wall for the tile design to be recognizable, but let sofa and floor establish depth. This should feel like entering a complete architecture, not a product close-up. The low furniture stays below most of the tile surface. Keep lower left relatively calm for a small website caption.
Lighting: soft neutral afternoon side light, restrained long shadows and crisp natural textures, organic slightly imperfect linen, polished editorial quality, balanced exposure with warm-neutral white balance, no orange filter.
Constraints: One complete living room. No people, logo, text, watermark, framed images, collage, collage panels, television, plants obscuring the tile or added ornament. Preserve the exact source sample design, pattern proportions, colors and surface relief; no fictitious embossed lattice. This is a fictional concept visualization using supplied product imagery, not a documented completed project.
